court_name: Superior Court of California, County of Monterey
case_search_note: Self-service records portal (linked from the court's Case Search page): current and completed cases back to 2008, no registration; view case info or scheduled hearings and pay criminal/traffic fines. Daily calendars: https://portal.monterey.courts.ca.gov/calendars/final-daily.

courthouses.name: Salinas Courthouse
courthouses.note: Courtrooms 1–11. Court lists cases served as Criminal, Juvenile and Mental Health and calls it the main hub (criminal, civil, family, probate, traffic). Main criminal courthouse; criminal clerk's office. Salinas Self-Help Center open Wednesdays 9–3.

courthouses.name: Marina Courthouse
courthouses.note: Courtrooms 20–21. Traffic services and traffic court hearings, night court, small claims, child support hearings. Traffic matters only (not felony/misdemeanor per the court's listing). Mailing: P.O. Box 2010, Marina, CA 93933.

courthouses.name: King City Courthouse
courthouses.note: Courtroom 18. Traffic payments and filings, traffic arraignments, family and restraining-order filings, small claims filings, child support calendars, self-help (Tuesdays 9–3). Traffic only for criminal-type matters.

courthouses.name: Monterey Courthouse
courthouses.note: Courtrooms 13–17. Civil, family, probate, jury services, family court services, self-help (Mon–Fri 9–4). Not criminal.

courthouses.name: Juvenile Justice Court
courthouses.note: Juvenile justice sessions held daily in the Juvenile Court Branch at the Probation Department; filings are kept at the Salinas Courthouse clerk's office. Not adult criminal.

public_defenders.name: Monterey County Public Defender
public_defenders.note: Fax (831) 755-5873. The Clear My Record page gives the email as askpubdef@co.monterey.ca.us.

legal_aid.name: Monterey County Public Defender — Clear My Record
legal_aid.serves: People with Monterey County criminal records
legal_aid.what: Free help from the Public Defender's office clearing a criminal record; call, email or visit the office.
legal_aid.todo: Eligibility details and services list not captured

legal_aid.name: Monterey Superior Court Self-Help Center
legal_aid.what: Information and form help (family law, restraining orders, evictions, small claims, etc.); no legal advice. Monterey (1200 Aguajito Rd) Mon–Fri 9–4; Salinas Wed 9–3; King City Tue 9–3. Form-completion help by phone appointment.

programs.name: Collaborative Courts
programs.summary: Court lists DUI/DWI Court, Drug Treatment Court, Mental Health Court (Creating New Choices) and Veterans Treatment Court — judicial supervision plus treatment instead of traditional incarceration, for those who qualify. Ask your attorney.

programs.name: Work Alternative Program (WAP)
programs.summary: Court says people sentenced to 40 days or less of jail may be eligible to serve it as community service through the Sheriff's Work Alternative Program.

programs.name: Supervised Home Confinement (Probation)
programs.summary: Custodial home-supervision program for non-violent offenders run by Probation as an alternative to county jail; participants apply and are monitored at home, school and work.

programs.name: Theft Offender / Assaultive Behavior classes
programs.summary: 8-hour classes a judge may order as part of pretrial diversion or sentencing for minor theft or assault offenses; registration fee paid to the program.

jails.name: Monterey County Jail (Main Jail and Rehabilitation Facility)
jails.phone_note: Sheriff's Office main number/address shown on the Sheriff's site; jail ADA coordinator (831) 755-3743; property releases (831) 755-3782. Mail goes through Smart Communications (P.O. Box 9199, Seminole, FL 33775-9199) with name and booking number. Public visiting rules are on the Jail Information page.
jails.court_ids_note: Court's Clerk's Office page says that if the DA files within 48 hours the Sheriff transports the defendant to court for arraignment; Sheriff also notes a limited video arraignment program. Salinas is the criminal courthouse (nearest; specific courtroom not confirmed).
jails.todo: Sheriff pages give 1414 Natividad Rd as the Sheriff's Office address; a separate street address for the jail buildings was not shown. Jail Division says the County Jail houses sentenced and unsentenced male and female persons (~1,100 in 31 housing units). Trust deposits: lobby kiosk, web.connectnetwork.com, or mail; fees apply.

bail.note: Before paying a bail agent, check that their license is active using the California Department of Insurance license lookup (search by name or license number). Monterey Superior Court bail and fee schedules: https://www.monterey.courts.ca.gov/forms-filing/bail-fee-schedules. The Sheriff's Jail Information page links an online bail payment service. Booking numbers are on the Sheriff's In Custody Log. The Public Defender's site also links a 'County Jail Inmate Locator' at montereysheriff.org/inmates/ (not verified as current). This is information only, not legal advice.
